mainEntity.name: How much does it cost to replace a GLC 220d or GLC 250d engine in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A GLC 220d or GLC 250d engine replacement typically costs between £2,200 and £3,900 depending on condition type and whether fitting is included. OM651 2.1-litre diesel units range from £2,200 to £3,900 supply only. Rebuilt OM651 (GLC 220d / 250d): £2,200-£3,900 supply only. Reconditioned units: £1,800-£3,200. Used engines from breakers: £1,200-£2,800 but higher risk. Labour for supply & fit adds £800-£1,500 to any engine price.

mainEntity.name: Is the OM651 engine in the GLC 220d and 250d reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The OM651 is fundamentally reliable - 200,000-300,000 km examples are common - but has predictable weak points. Timing chain stretch from ~120,000 km - the single most critical failure point. Piezo injector wear from neglected oil changes. EGR clogging from short journeys. Water pump leaks on higher-mileage units. With regular servicing (10,000 miles / 12 months with MB 229.51/229.52 oil), these engines regularly exceed 250,000 miles.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of OM651 timing chain failure in a GLC diesel?

acceptedAnswer.text: The OM651's timing chain typically shows warning signs before complete failure. Rattling or clanking noise on cold start - the earliest warning sign. Rattle that lasts more than 2-3 seconds indicates significant chain stretch. Check engine light with cam/crank correlation codes (P0016/P0017). If ignored, the chain can jump teeth and destroy the engine.

mainEntity.name: Should I repair or replace my GLC 220d or 250d engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Repair if the failure is isolated (e.g., timing chain tensioner, injectors, EGR cleaning). Replace if there's bottom end damage, bore scoring, or catastrophic timing chain failure. Timing chain tensioner replacement at specialist: £350-£600 - do this at first sign of rattle. Injector cleaning: £200-£350 - excellent value for warm-start issues. Full OM651 rebuild: £3,200-£5,000 - for catastrophic failure or 120k+ miles. Given GLC 220d / 250d values (£12,000-£25,000), a rebuilt engine is typically good value.

acceptedAnswer.text: Check your vehicle log book (V5C) for the engine number, which includes the engine code prefix. V5C log book shows full engine number with code prefix. Engine code stamped on cylinder block. GLC 220d (2015-2019): OM651.924 (2.1L diesel, 170hp). GLC 250d (2015-2019): OM651.921 (2.1L diesel, 204hp). Service history documents list engine type.

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes Benz GLC Class 220d / 250d Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Mercedes Benz GLC 220d and 250d rely on the OM651 2.1-litre twin-turbo diesel - a fundamentally robust engine that regularly exceeds 200,000-300,000 km when properly maintained, but has developed a well-documented reputation for predictable failures. Timing chain stretch, piezo injector wear, swirl flap actuator failure, and water pump leaks are the most frequently cited issues. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components designed to address the original failure point - plus a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty. Below we break down the most common GLC 220d and 250d engine failures, what they cost to fix, and when replacement is the smarter financial decision.

problems.h4: OM651 Timing Chain Stretch - Why the GLC 220d / 250d Rattles on Cold Start
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes Benz GLC Class GLC 220d (OM651.924) and GLC 250d (OM651.921), 2015-2019
problems.rootCause: The OM651's single-row timing chain drives both camshafts and the high-pressure fuel pump. A faulty chain tensioner causes premature chain elongation, producing a distinct rattle during cold starts. If ignored, chain skip can lead to cam/crank correlation codes, misfires, and catastrophic engine damage.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain tensioner and guides only - valid if caught immediately when rattle first appears
repairOptions.longevity: Effective only if addressed within first 500-1,000 miles of noise

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain, tensioner, guides, sprockets - labour intensive
repairOptions.longevity: 80k-120k miles; corrects the root cause properly

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt OM651 with new timing components, upgraded tensioner, new injectors, full gasket set
repairOptions.longevity: Full long-block warranty. Required if chain has jumped or guides have failed

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical GLC 220d or 250d (X253, 2015-2019) is worth £12,000-£25,000 depending on age, mileage and condition - the full replacement cost of £3,200-£5,000 is modest relative to vehicle value for most examples. For vehicles worth under £10,000, evaluate repair options first.
problems.recommendation: If you hear the characteristic 2-3 second rattle only on cold start with no fault codes, replace the tensioner immediately - it's £350-£600 well spent. Once chain skip triggers camshaft correlation codes (P0016/P0017), the full timing kit is mandatory. If the engine has jumped timing causing valve contact, only a full replacement engine makes financial sense. With proper maintenance, OM651 diesels can exceed 250,000-300,000 miles.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt OM651 Mercedes Benz GLC Class 220d / 250d engine prices

problems.h4: OM651 Piezo Injector Failure - Why the GLC 220d / 250d Starts Poorly When Warm
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes Benz GLC Class GLC 220d (OM651.924) and GLC 250d (OM651.921), 2015-2019
problems.rootCause: The OM651's piezo injectors are prone to premature wear-and-tear and a high failure rate, particularly when oil change intervals are neglected. Carbon deposits form around the injector nozzle tip and sealing washer, disrupting the spray pattern and allowing combustion gases to blow past - leading to hard starting when warm, rough idle, and misfires.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Ultrasonic injector cleaning, carbon removal from injector bores, new sealing washers
repairOptions.longevity: 80k-100k miles. Viable for minor warm-start issues

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace failed piezo injectors, code to ECU, decarbonise affected cylinders
repairOptions.longevity: 80k-120k miles. Required when cleaning no longer resolves issues

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt OM651 with new injectors, timing chain, decarbonised head
repairOptions.longevity: Full long-block warranty. Necessary when injector bore damage or multiple injector failure

problems.vehicleValueCheck: On a GLC 220d or 250d worth £12,000-£25,000, replacing individual injectors as they fail is sensible. However, piezo injectors are expensive (£300-£500 each new), so replacing all four on a car over 100,000 miles pushes costs towards £1,200-£2,000. At that point, compare the cost against a full rebuilt engine with new injectors included.
problems.recommendation: If your GLC 220d or 250d takes three or four cranks to start when warm but runs fine once going, start with professional injector cleaning at a diesel specialist - £200-£350 often solves it. However, piezo injectors are expensive, so consider a full rebuilt engine if you're facing multiple injector failures on a high-mileage car.
problems.cta: -> Compare OM651 injector replacement and rebuilt engine prices for your GLC 220d / 250d

problems.group: OM651 Swirl Flap Actuator & EGR Failure
problems.h4: OM651 Swirl Flap Actuator & EGR Failure - Why the GLC 220d / 250d Loses Power and Triggers Emissions Faults
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes Benz GLC Class GLC 220d (OM651.924) and GLC 250d (OM651.921), 2015-2019
problems.rootCause: The intake port shutoff (swirl flap) actuator can fail, affecting EGR operation and causing power loss and emissions faults. EGR clogging from short journeys is also common.

repairOptions.tier: Minor - EGR Valve & Swirl Flap Cleaning
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove and clean EGR valve, swirl flaps, clear carbon deposits, reset adaptations
Replace swirl flap actuator, new seals, recalibrate
Supply & fit rebuilt OM651 with new EGR system, swirl flaps, decarbonised intake
repairOptions.longevity: Full long-block warranty. For catastrophic failure or 120k+ miles

problems.vehicleValueCheck: On a GLC 220d or 250d worth £12,000-£25,000, EGR cleaning at £200-£400 is excellent preventative maintenance. Full engine replacement is only justified for catastrophic failure.
problems.recommendation: The OM651's EGR and swirl flap systems benefit from regular carbon cleaning, particularly on urban-driven vehicles. If you notice rough idle or loss of power, have the EGR valve and intake system inspected. Specialist cleaning is significantly cheaper than dealer pricing and can restore lost performance.
